review_notes: I read all 120 lines of the file, plus the definitions and lemmas it depends on: `lowJet` (LowJetChainRule.lean), `variationLowJet`, `lowJet_affine` and `weighted_variationLowJet` (JetVariations.lean), `WeightedBound`, `.deriv_le` and `.congr` (WeightedBounds.lean), `weightedBound_comp_isometry` and `planeCoordinateIsometry` (SupportedCoordinateChange.lean), and `weightedBound_comp_isometry_on` (LocalIsometryBounds.lean). A grep found no uses of these declarations outside this file. The two `rpow` ratio lemmas are already general. `weighted_increment_unscaled` already works for any set `U`. The `ContDiff ℝ ∞` hypotheses in `lowJet_increment_eq_variation` come from what `lowJet_affine` requires, so weakening them would need new API work. I considered stating the `Set.univ` lemmas for open sets, using `weightedBound_comp_isometry_on`, and stating them for arbitrary isometries. I did not report either, because neither has a demonstrated use and both would add abstraction without a clear benefit. I also considered weakening the family hypothesis `hWb` in `primitive_slow_increment_bounds`. I did not report it: the theorem's second conjunct is quantified over every order, so bounds at every order are a natural input there. I could not compile any of the proposed replacements; the proof sketches below follow the existing proof steps.

findings.excerpt:
(lowJet (fun y => G y + H y) x - lowJet G x) (.inl i) = 0 := by
  change x i - x i = 0
findings.problem: The statement only covers the additive update `fun y => G y + H y`, but the additive structure plays no part in the proof. By definition, `lowJet F p (Sum.inl i) = p i` for every map `F`, so the position coordinates of `lowJet F x - lowJet G x` are zero for any two maps `F` and `G`. The proof (`change x i - x i = 0; exact sub_self _`) never looks at `H`.
findings.proposed_change: State it for arbitrary maps: `lemma lowJet_sub_lowJet_position (F G : JetPolynomial.Base → JetPolynomial.Space) (x : JetPolynomial.Base) (i : Fin 2) : (lowJet F x - lowJet G x) (.inl i) = 0 := by change x i - x i = 0; exact sub_self _`. The current version is the special case `F := fun y => G y + H y`. There are no other call sites to update.
findings.benefit: The lemma then applies to any two maps being compared, for example non-additive coordinate changes or rescaled updates, not just additive increments. It also shows the reader that position cancellation is a property of `lowJet` itself, not of the update.

findings.excerpt:
(hWb : ∀ m, WeightedBound Set.univ (z ^ b) m
      (S m * z ^ d * z ^ b) W) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ 3) (x : JetPolynomial.Base) :
findings.problem: The conclusion is a bound on derivatives of order at most 3 with constant `S 3`. Even so, the lemma asks for a weighted bound on `W` at every order `m`, plus a whole sequence `S : ℕ → ℝ` that is nonnegative everywhere. It goes through `primitive_slow_increment_bounds`, whose first conjunct uses only `hWb 3` and `hS 3` (via `slow_increment_C3`). A caller who only has a C³ bound on `W` cannot use the lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the family with one order-3 bound: `lemma primitive_slow_increment_derivative {G : JetPolynomial.Base → JetPolynomial.Space} {W : RealModes.RField 4} (hW : ContDiff ℝ ∞ W) {z d b S : ℝ} (hz : 0 < z) (hz1 : z ≤ 1) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hS : 0 ≤ S) (hWb : WeightedBound Set.univ (z ^ b) 3 (S * z ^ d * z ^ b) W) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ 3) (x : JetPolynomial.Base) : ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j ((fun y => G y + W (planeCoordinateIsometry y)) - G) x‖ ≤ S * z ^ (d - 2 * b)`. Proof: derive `hτ`, `hτ1` and `hδ` as on lines 91–93. Then take `hh := slow_increment_C3 hW hτ hτ1 hδ hS hWb`, `rw [slow_increment_C3_ratio hz] at hh`, transfer it to the increment with `hh.congr` and `add_sub_cancel_left`, and finish with `hh j hj x (Set.mem_univ x)` and `simpa only [one_pow, one_mul, iteratedFDerivWithin_univ]`. If `G` is ever not smooth, `hG` is no longer needed, because `slow_increment_C3` does not use it. The degenerate case `j = 0` (sup norm) is still covered by `hj : j ≤ 3`.
findings.benefit: Callers that only control `W` up to order 3 can use the lemma. Callers with a family of bounds can still apply it with `hWb 3` and `hS 3`. The statement also shows that the C³ estimate depends only on third-order control.
